product.title: areas, water, places and peaks (the base map bands)

standing.claim: A failed Census population download is not a failed kind, so the state reads loaded with no problem sentence, and the map receives a literal None kind.
standing.evidence: build() records the download failure only in ctx.failures (line 1581), never in failed['place']. The state at line 1740 ignores ctx.failures, and map_data_vector takes row.get('kind') (line 1945). Experiment X3b (full run without --box, mt2020.pl.zip absent from the cache): state 'loaded', problem null, failures [{source: census_pl2020}] with no kind, map failed_kinds ['None']. D16 (docstring lines 93-95) requires the kind named and state partial. The parse failure (line 1579) is recorded under place, so the download and parse paths disagree. In experiment X3 every test place then shows population null and rank null, with no partial sentence to explain it.
standing.fix: On a missing population file, append the reason to failed['place'] so the state is partial and the place kind is named, using WORDS['population_unknown'] or a place sentence. Give ctx.failures rows a kind, and drop rows without one in map_data_vector.

standing.claim: The five P2 zip fixtures are git-ignored and absent from the branch tree, so the basemap2 tests error on a clean checkout.
standing.evidence: The rule '*.zip' (line 8) ignores tests/fixtures/basemap2/*.zip (git check-ignore confirms). git ls-tree -r HEAD lists no .zip file. tests/test_basemap2.py reads them through _fixture (line 33). ReaderTests (line 221) and BuildTests (line 303) skip only when pyshp is missing, and website.yml line 111 installs pyshp, so in CI they would fail with FileNotFoundError rather than skip. The same rule hides P3's tests/fixtures/landmarks/tiger_arealm_mt_sample.zip.
standing.fix: git add -f the five zips in the commit, or add a negation (!tests/fixtures/**/*.zip) to .gitignore in the same change. Tell the P3 owner about the landmarks zip.

standing.claim: Reservations, routes, parks and summit heights that come back empty after filtering are not recorded as failures, so the state reads loaded with nothing drawn.
standing.evidence: inputs['reservations'] (line 1564), inputs['routes'] (line 1571), inputs['parks'] (line 1615) and the peaks (line 1706) are set even when empty, with no failure entry. Experiment X11: a road file with only county roads gives routes [] with no route failure, sources tiger_prisec 'cache', and verify ok True. Experiment X7: forest names that do not match leave forests at 0 with no forest failure; only the verify check fails. verify's named checks (lines 1913-1928) cover reservations, forests, two rivers, two places and McDonald Peak, but nothing checks that route shields or parks are present. sample_elevations returns None for every summit without recording a problem (lines 1693-1706), so all summits count as no height and the state still reads loaded.
standing.fix: After each source, if the usable count is zero, append a named failure (for example failed['route'].append('the road file gave no interstate, US or state routes')) so the state is partial. Add verify checks that route shields and parks are present.

standing.claim: fetch_pages takes an attempts argument but never passes it on, so every envelope query gets three tries and the one-try design above the last split level never runs.
standing.evidence: fetch_pages accepts attempts (line 704) and calls fetch at line 711 without it. Experiment X4: a 1-degree envelope where every response is HTTP 504 made 63 requests; the design in the comment at line 754 gives 53 (1 + 4 x 1 + 16 x 3). The builder's logs show each 504 took 70 to 180 s, so every failing envelope costs about ten extra requests.
standing.fix: Pass the argument through: fetch(ctx, source, url, page_name(...), _check_features, params=q, attempts=attempts). Add a test that counts the requests for a failing envelope.

standing.claim: An unreadable cache file crashes the build, although the docstring says such a file is a failed source, never a crash.
standing.evidence: fetch() calls path.read_bytes() without a guard (line 346). Experiment X6 with PermissionError on the cache file: the build crashed for mt2020.pl.zip (called from build() at line 1575, outside attempt()), for the NHD small-lines page (line 1620) and for the 3DEP batch (line 1695, via line 804). Band D (line 1658) and small areas (line 1629) take the same unguarded path, by reading the code. Module docstring line 98 makes the promise.
standing.fix: Catch OSError around the cache read and treat the file as unusable, so the request path runs and the reason is recorded. Or wrap the remaining direct calls in attempt(), as the TIGER calls already are.

standing.claim: A store index with no tiles raises BasemapError and writes no D20 block, although the docstring and integration.md say the product becomes unavailable.
standing.evidence: build() raises at lines 1535-1536, and _read_json raises when the index is missing (line 1533). Experiment X2: BasemapError 'the store index lists no tiles', and no vector index is written. main() (line 1979) has no handler, so the CLI prints a traceback. Docstring lines 98-103 and integration.md section 6 say the product is unavailable with its files removed. The workflow's unavailable fallback on a non-zero exit limits the practical risk.
standing.fix: Call mark_unavailable(store, reason) and return its dict, as the all-failed path does (lines 1710-1714). Or catch BasemapError in main() and call mark_unavailable.

standing.claim: Band files carry no piece size and no feature identity, so the label rule that the docstring and integration.md describe cannot be applied.
standing.evidence: encode() (lines 1256-1265) drops size. The docstring (lines 40-42) says a browser can label the longest piece of a name, and integration.md (lines 140-141) says to label 'on the piece with the largest size' and that band files carry it. Experiment X5: band A feature keys are g, k, l, n, z only. The label point goes only to the piece whose cell holds it (line 1342), so the largest piece may carry no label. The output has no feature id. In the statewide output, 163 (kind, name, zoom) combinations carry two or more label points, which must be separate features with the same name (for example Big Lake at zoom 8 in n44w110 and n46w112, and Dry Lake at zoom 9 in five labelled pieces). The once-per-view rule would hide one of each pair.
standing.fix: Write size and a feature id (the source OBJECTID) on every piece, and state that the label sits on the piece with l. Or drop the once-per-view rule for areas. Make the docstring and integration.md match whichever is chosen.

standing.claim: The statewide band D run is incomplete, and the request unit differs from the brief: large-scale water is requested per 1-degree cell, not per tile.
standing.evidence: The brief's P2 paragraph and research/map-b6/README.md line 171 both say large-scale per tile. build() requests one envelope per 1-degree cell (lines 1644-1652), a choice not recorded as a decision. measurements.json band_d_cold_run: 2 of 54 cells completed, 20 of 4,597 tiles built, and the band D budget is measured on those 20 shards only. The builder's own one-record probe also timed out, so the unit alone may not explain the 504s; the per-tile form has not been tested.
standing.fix: Either request per tile as briefed and measure, or record the change and its reason in the report. Finish the statewide band D run from the cache before phase B, and report the band D budget on the full set.

standing.claim: The 57 tests pass, but none pins the failure paths that the other findings describe.
standing.evidence: No test covers: a failed population download (P2-01); empty routes, parks or forests after filtering (P2-03); the retry count (P2-04); an unreadable cache file (P2-05); the no-tiles D20 path (P2-06); the size key on pieces (P2-07); the sentence with four or more failed kinds (P2-12); or verify's river checks when only band D water failed (P2-14). AGENTS.md requires tests with every behaviour change.
standing.fix: Add one offline test per item, using the existing fixture builder and stubbed fetches.

standing.claim: The McDonald Peak check does not cite a named reference, and the module says the research record names one, which it does not.
standing.evidence: The published figure (9,824 ft, 2,994.4 m) is the Wikipedia infobox figure, which cites Peakbagger (pid 4705); the article text gives 9,820 ft (2,993 m). The source is landmarks/terrain-rivers/dl/021-wikipedia-peaks/wiki_McDonald_Peak.html. research/map-b6/README.md does not mention the peak. The test (tests/test_basemap2.py lines 255-262) passes with the 3DEP sample of 2969.2 m, which is 25.2 m below the figure against a 30 m tolerance.
standing.fix: Name the reference in PEAK_CHECK (Peakbagger, reached through the Wikipedia article, with the access date), give both listed figures, and keep the 30 m check. Correct the sentence saying the research record names the reference.

standing.claim: The partial-failure sentence says 'stations' for map kinds when more than three kinds fail.
standing.evidence: _named() calls stations._named_list (website/stations.py lines 1518-1523; UNREAD_NAMES_SHOWN = 3 at line 964). Experiment X1 output: 'reservation outlines, forest outlines, park outlines and 2 more stations'.
standing.fix: Write a local join for map kinds (for example 'and 2 more map kinds') instead of calling the station helper.

standing.claim: The module header says quotes come from the sources' own metadata, but the 3DEP quote came from a secondary copy.
standing.evidence: Lines 90-91 quote the 3DEP statement. cartography/proof/sources.json, source 0: 'Public domain: verified in a secondary copy; primary USGS page not reachable'. The primary copyrights page returned HTTP 403.
standing.fix: Say that the 3DEP line is from a secondary copy of the USGS statement, or read the primary page before the About page ships.

standing.claim: verify skips both river checks whenever any water fails, although both rivers are in bands A and B, which loaded.
standing.evidence: named() (lines 1906-1911) skips on any water failure. In the statewide offline build (52 band D cells failed), the output holds Clark Fork (zooms 5 and 6) and Bitterroot River (zoom 6) in v/a.json, and both at zooms 8 and 9 in v/b/n46w114.json and v/b/n44w116.json. verify reports 'not checked: water did not load in this build'.
standing.fix: Skip a river check only when the bands that could hold the river failed, or record water failures per band.

standing.claim: The measured figures behind the river rule (54,026 gzip bytes; 52,291 and 121,622 streams; 124 features) are not recorded anywhere.
standing.evidence: They are not in measurements.json or in any log under build/P2 or cartography/landmarks. The matches for those digits are hashes and coordinates.
standing.fix: Record the measurements, with the command and the file, in measurements.json, or remove the figures from the docstring and the DECISIONS text.

standing.claim: Park labels take the agency's name when the location name is blank, and placeholder names reach the map.
standing.evidence: The live PAD-US cache has five SP rows with Unit_Nm 'Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks' and a blank Loc_Nm, so park_name returns the unit name. It also has five rows named 'Unknown Park' (four LP, one SREC).
standing.fix: Treat a blank or placeholder name as no name, and leave that park unlabelled. Do not use the agency name as a park's name.

standing.claim: The coverage sentence gives box coordinates with no unit and no order.
standing.evidence: WORDS['coverage_box'] is formatted with the box as '-114.1, 46.8, -113.9, 47' (lines 1742-1743).
standing.fix: Say it in words with degrees and the order, for example 'from 114.1 W to 113.9 W and from 46.8 N to 47 N'.

standing.claim: The build command makes --cache required; the brief says the P2 commands are as in P1, where --cache is optional.
standing.evidence: build_parser line 1963 sets required=True. The brief's P1 command line shows [--cache DIR].
standing.fix: Default the cache to a folder under the store, or record the deviation in the report.

standing.claim: Two missing values become zero: a river with no drainage area is dropped as 0 km2, and a park with no acreage gets size 0.
standing.evidence: Line 1627 uses _num(...) or 0.0 for TOTDASQKM, and line 1614 does the same for GIS_ACRES. The server filter TotDASqKM >= 100 (line 203) keeps nulls out today, so the risk is latent.
standing.fix: Keep None, count the row as unusable and report the count, rather than writing 0.

standing.claim: Three WORDS entries are never used by the module.
standing.evidence: part_unavailable (line 234), peaks_unknown (line 238) and population_unknown (line 240) have no use in basemap2.py. population_unknown is the sentence the population failure needs (P2-01).
standing.fix: Use them in build() where the failures are reported, or delete them and say that the integrator formats them.

notes: P2-02 (.gitignore) and P2-24 (website.yml) are the integrator's: write the exact lines into integration.md (a negation !tests/fixtures/**/*.zip for the fixtures; the five test modules in on.push.paths and the offline line); edit no shared file. P2-07: write size and a feature id (the source OBJECTID) on every piece and state that the label sits on the piece with l; docstring and integration.md follow. P2-08: do not re-run the statewide band D now; record the per-cell request unit and its reason (the skeptics measured that per-tile requests would take roughly 24 to 47 hours serially while a cell answers in one request when the service is up) as a decision in report.md and integration.md; band D is optional for the first release (the browser draws band C's water at zoom 13 and up until a tile's shard exists) and the monthly job continues it under a 20-minute step cap from the cache. P2-11: name the reference (Peakbagger, reached through the Wikipedia article, with the access date) and both listed figures in PEAK_CHECK. P2-12: name every failed kind in the partial sentence (seven short names at most), with no cap and no count. P2-13: say the 3DEP statement is quoted from a secondary copy of the USGS text, as website/terrain.py does. P2-14: skip a river check only when the bands that could hold the river (A and B) failed. P2-15: remove the unrecorded figures from the docstring (no re-measurement now) and say the river rule's threshold without them. P2-16: a park with a blank or placeholder name (Unknown Park, or the agency name Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks in the unit field with a blank location name) keeps its outline and gets no name and no label point; the gate must not drop it; a test. P2-19: make --cache optional with a default folder beside the store. P2-21: keep None for a missing drainage area or acreage: a river with no area is left out and counted as unusable in the index; a park with no acreage keeps its outline with size None (ordered last when a file is over budget) and is counted; never write 0; a test. P2-23: use the WORDS entries where the failures are reported (population_unknown for P2-01) and delete the ones that stay unused. The forest credit line reads 'Source: USDA Forest Service, forest boundaries (national forests).'
